papers.title: Drug Repositioning in Kinase Inhibitor Discovery for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Repurposing of existing drugs has emerged as a time- and cost-effective strategy in oncology drug discovery. Given the critical role of dysregulated kinase signaling in cancer, kinase-focused repurposing strategies have attracted considerable interest. This approach encompasses both "target hopping" between different kinases and the discovery of unexpected kinase inhibitory activity in non-kinase drugs. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the repositioning of kinase inhibitors from medicinal chemistry and structural biology perspectives. We highlight the structural basis and bindin
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent strategies for repurposing existing drugs as kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy, focusing on two approaches: 'target hopping' between kinases and discovering unexpected kinase inhibitory activity in non-kinase drugs. It highlights the structural biology and medicinal chemistry basis of binding and selectivity, providing a framework for accelerating kinase inhibitor discovery.

papers.title: Proprietary Cationic Lipo-Oligopeptides Inhibit Herpes Simplex Virus-1 Infection.
papers.abstract: The use of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) infection has surged amidst the rise of HSV-1 drug-resistant strains. AMPs offer an unconventional approach to combat HSV-1 infection by exerting their activity on multiple phases of the viral life cycle, while exhibiting low rates of resistance emergence. In this study, an integrated in silico and in vitro approach was used to evaluate six proprietary cationic lipo-oligopeptides (CLOPs) (P226, P359, P577, P581, OB1105, and OB1111) as potential anti-HSV-1 agents. Computational tools were used to predict vari
papers.summary: This study evaluated six proprietary cationic lipo-oligopeptides (CLOPs) as potential anti-HSV-1 agents using a combined computational and in vitro approach. The peptides were screened in silico for antiviral properties and then tested experimentally against HSV-1 infection, with the goal of identifying alternatives to conventional drugs amid rising drug-resistant HSV-1 strains. The work represents an early-stage preclinical evaluation of these compounds as candidate antiviral peptides.

papers.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit
papers.summary: This review discusses how LC-MS metabolomic profiling, combined with expanding spectral databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation, is improving the characterization of complex natural product metabolomes. It highlights how AI-enabled navigation of natural product chemical space can help overcome low annotation rates and rediscovery of known metabolites, accelerating natural product-based drug discovery and biotechnology.

papers.title: Evaluation of Physics-Based Pose Prediction and the Role of Receptor Flexibility in a Community Antiviral Blind Challenge.
papers.abstract: Prediction of protein-ligand binding modes is a key step in computer-aided drug design, since incorrect pose prediction inevitably limits the achievable accuracy of downstream physics-based affinity predictions. The ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral competition was launched in 2025 as a means to prospectively test computational methods across a range of measurements that guide early prioritization during a drug discovery campaign including pose prediction. Here, we describe our two open-source, physics-based entries to the pose prediction challenge, which are based on templated molecular growth
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper reports two open-source, physics-based methods for protein-ligand pose prediction that were entered into the 2025 ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral blind challenge. The methods use templated molecular growth and explicitly account for receptor flexibility, and the study evaluates their performance in a prospective community setting.

papers.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a new organic-inorganic copper(II) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], and characterized its crystal structure, which features discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions held together by hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and halogen contacts. Optical measurements show semiconducting behavior with a ~2.5 eV band gap and broad visible emission, and the work is complemented by DFT, molecular docking, and biological assays. The study links the material's supramolecular structure to its optical and bioactivity properties.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. This narrative review (PubMed/MEDLINE searched through August 2026, supplemented by hand-searching and conference abstracts) appraises the evidence for AI applications across the MPN continuum. Artificial intelligence (AI), and its principal subfields, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), learn predictive patterns directly from data rather than from explicitly programmed rules,
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys the evidence for artificial intelligence applications across the myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) care continuum, from digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support. It covers how machine learning and deep learning can integrate heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data to aid diagnosis, prognostication, and management. The review is intended as a synthesis of current evidence rather than a primary study.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules that combine paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were structurally characterized and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking supporting the binding to COX targets.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which proteins might mediate the anticancer (cytotoxic) effects of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus plants. No new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target identification. The findings propose candidate molecular targets that could guide future experimental validation of these natural products.

papers.title: LASSBio-classFLOW: A Semiautomated KNIME Workflow for Classification Model Benchmarking and Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Machine learning-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (ML-QSAR) modeling requires consistent data preparation, validation, and model comparison. We present LASSBio-classFLOW, an open, modular, and semiautomated KNIME workflow for classification-based ligand screening. It integrates basic molecular structure preparation, configurable class assignment, descriptors and fingerprints calculation, dataset partitioning, hyperparameter optimization of nine algorithms, interactive performance evaluation, user-guided model selection, and external-library prediction. As an example, the work
papers.summary: LASSBio-classFLOW is an open, modular KNIME workflow that semi-automates the entire ML-QSAR pipeline for classification-based ligand screening, from molecular preparation and descriptor calculation through hyperparameter optimization of nine algorithms to model evaluation and virtual screening of external libraries. It provides a reusable, user-guided framework that standardizes data preparation, validation, and model comparison, lowering the barrier to reproducible QSAR modeling.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting amyloidogenic sequences to structural biology and inhibitor/drug design for neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It organizes the field into key application domains and evaluates progress and remaining challenges in using ML to understand and target amyloid-forming polypeptides.

papers.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitory evaluation of prenylated flavonoids from peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) shells: in vitro and in silico molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Sustainable agriculture has become a crucial priority because the improper management of agricultural waste currently contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, as well as soil and air pollution. The shells of Arachis hypogaea L., which is commonly discarded as an agricultural by-product, have been reported to contain various secondary metabolites, including flavonoids, stilbenes, triterpenoids, etc. This work led to the isolation of two new prenylated flavonoids, arachisflavones A (1) and B (2), together with five prenylated flavones (3-7), two prenylated chalcones (8-9), and three prenylated f
papers.summary: This study isolated two new prenylated flavonoids (arachisflavones A and B) along with several known prenylated flavones and chalcones from peanut shells, an agricultural waste product. The compounds were tested for xanthine oxidase inhibition in vitro and evaluated via molecular docking, identifying peanut shell flavonoids as potential natural xanthine oxidase inhibitors with relevance to gout or oxidative stress management.

papers.title: Rational design and synthesis of furan-based Schiff base quinazolin-4-amine hybrids: spectral elucidation, molecular docking, DFT studies, and in silico ADMET-antioxidant study.
papers.abstract: In this work, a new series of furan-based quinazoline-4-amine hydrazone (Schiff base) derivatives (4a-h) was rationally designed and synthesized in good yields (84-90%) through a multistep route involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, and hydrazone/Schiff base condensation reactions. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and ESI-mass spectrometry, which confirmed the proposed structures. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to optimize the molecular geometries and to derive frontier molecular orbital
papers.summary: This paper reports the rational design and synthesis of eight new furan-based quinazolin-4-amine Schiff base hybrids using a multistep route (nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, and hydrazone condensation), with structures confirmed by FT-IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. The authors use DFT calculations to optimize geometries and derive frontier molecular orbital properties, and perform molecular docking plus in silico ADMET and antioxidant predictions to assess the compounds' drug-likeness and potential bioactivity.

papers.title: NU-1025 modulates immunogenic cell death in bladder cancer: A multi-omics insight.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has shown limited efficacy in bladder cancer, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) can stimulate adaptive immunity and remodel the tumor microenvironment, yet its comprehensive landscape and druggable potential in bladder cancer remain unexplored. Here, we performed integrative bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO bladder cancer cohorts to characterize ICD-associated subtypes, construct a prognostic risk model, and analyze immune infiltration. Connectivity Map (CMa
papers.summary: This study used integrative bioinformatics on TCGA and GEO bladder cancer transcriptomes to characterize immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated subtypes, build a prognostic risk model, and profile immune infiltration. The authors then used Connectivity Map analysis to identify NU-1025 as a compound that may modulate ICD in bladder cancer. The work is exploratory and computational, with no experimental validation reported in the abstract.

papers.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware fe
papers.summary: This study builds a computational drug discovery pipeline that combines machine learning on pathway-level features from 16 RA GEO datasets with target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and in vitro testing to find natural small molecules against rheumatoid arthritis. The framework uses GSVA-derived pathway features for cohort-aware modeling and reserves one dataset for independent validation. It represents an integrated, multi-step approach to repurpose natural compounds for RA.

papers.title: Computational Identification of GABA-A Receptor Ligands Targeting the Histamine Allosteric Pocket.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor is a key regulator of inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and a promising target for cognitive and neurological disorders. Histamine interacts with a distinct allosteric pocket located at the β3-β3 subunit interface, providing an opportunity for the discovery of novel ligands. In the present study, an integrated in silico workflow combining ligand-based similarity analysis, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was applied to identify candidate ligands for this histamine-associated site. D
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline—ligand similarity screening, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify candidate small molecules that bind the histamine allosteric pocket at the β3-β3 interface of the GABA-A receptor. The work proposes novel ligand candidates for this under-explored site, which could inform future development of compounds for cognitive and neurological disorders. Findings are purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara
papers.summary: This review examines how the close biological similarity between fungal pathogens and human cells—the "eukaryotic paradox"—complicates AI-driven drug repurposing efforts against antifungal resistance. It surveys computational strategies for overcoming this challenge, emphasizing the need to identify fungal-specific targets despite extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology with the human host.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
papers.abstract: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, na
papers.summary: This review proposes a three-part taxonomy for integrating mechanistic mathematical models with artificial intelligence in the life sciences. It argues that combining the explanatory rigor of hypothesis-driven modeling with AI's pattern-finding power on large, high-dimensional datasets can yield more predictive and personalized biology than either paradigm alone. The paper serves as a roadmap for how these two approaches can be synthesized.

papers.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA.
papers.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemen
papers.summary: This study builds a QSAR model from 20 known piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa inhibitors and uses it to prioritize 20 new analog designs, then validates the top candidates through docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA calculations against apixaban. The integrated computational workflow demonstrates a practical pipeline for triaging FXa inhibitor candidates before synthesis, though no experimental validation is reported.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc), using transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data, and spatial assays. The authors provide rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat as a therapeutic strategy targeting these fibroblast states. The work emphasizes donor-resolved inference and includes molecular dynamics simulations to support the proposed mechanism.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological prediction, and drug discovery. It highlights that traditional control strategies are limited by slow and biosafety-risky culture methods and by serological tests that cannot easily distinguish natural infection from vaccine-induced immunity, and argues that AI approaches may help address these gaps.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—combining machine learning regressors, hierarchical molecular docking, MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations—to virtually screen for novel MELK kinase inhibitors. The screen identified a lead compound that showed antiproliferative activity and induced G2/M cell cycle arrest in triple-negative breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma cell lines. The work demonstrates a machine-learning-guided virtual screening strategy for discovering structurally novel kinase inhibitors.

papers.title: Identifying Anticancer Peptide via a Semi-Supervised Prediction Framework with Bio-Inspired Augmentation.
papers.abstract: Anticancer peptides (ACPs) have emerged as a promising class of therapeutic molecules due to their low toxicity and high specificity. However, experimentally identifying ACPs is labor-intensive and low-throughput, making virtual screening with intelligent models an attractive alternative. Despite recent progress, the number of ACP samples available in existing databases remains limited, which may cause predictive models to overfit the labeled information and exhibit suboptimal generalization. To address this issue, we propose a semi-supervised prediction framework with bio-inspired data augmen
papers.summary: The authors present a semi-supervised machine learning framework for predicting anticancer peptides, addressing the scarcity of labeled training data by combining bio-inspired data augmentation with semi-supervised learning. This approach aims to improve generalization and reduce overfitting compared to models trained only on the limited labeled ACP datasets currently available. The work is a computational contribution to peptide-based drug discovery rather than an experimental or broadly transformative advance.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review outlines the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with the complementary roles of molecular docking and experimental validation. It argues that this systems-level framework helps overcome the challenges posed by the complex, multi-target nature of natural product bioactivity.

papers.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products.
papers.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph-language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core
papers.summary: The authors present NP-GUARD, a modular computational framework that combines explainable AI with database mining to prioritize natural products for antimicrobial activity testing. The approach frames antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem, integrating six core components to rank untested compounds. This could help focus experimental screening on the most promising candidates amid rising antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Background: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives: This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods: A literature s
papers.summary: This review surveys next-generation ALS disease models, arguing that conventional 2D cultures and animal models are insufficient for understanding pathogenesis and developing therapies. It highlights iPSC-derived 3D systems combined with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 editing, multi-omics, and AI/machine learning as transformative platforms that better recapitulate ALS hallmarks and could accelerate drug discovery.

papers.title: DeepAVPred: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating RECM-DWT and BiGRU for Accurate Antiviral Peptide Prediction.
papers.abstract: Viral infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge. Antiviral peptides (AVPs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their high specificity, favorable safety profiles, and broad-spectrum antiviral activity. However, experimental AVP identification is time-consuming and costly, while existing computational predictors often have limitations in predictive accuracy and feature representation. Here, we propose DeepAVPred, a deep learning-based framework for AVP identification. DeepAVPred integrates complementary sequence descriptors to capture physicochemical pro
papers.summary: DeepAVPred is a deep learning framework for identifying antiviral peptides from sequence data. It combines a new feature extraction method (RECM-DWT) with a bidirectional GRU network to capture both physicochemical properties and sequence context, aiming to improve on existing computational predictors that struggle with accuracy and feature representation. The work addresses the costly and slow experimental identification of antiviral peptides by offering a faster in silico alternative.

papers.title: In Silico Discovery of a Potential PI3Kα Inhibitor Incorporating an Imidazole Moiety for Breast Cancer Treatment.
papers.abstract: Excessive activation of PI3Kα is prevalent in breast cancer, aberrantly activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to drive tumor progression, thus rendering PI3Kα a vital therapeutic target. Two PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib and inavolisib) have been approved for clinical application. Inavolisib exerts a mutation-selective degradation mechanism and functions by directly eliminating aberrant proteins. To develop novel PI3Kα inhibitors, we employed multiple computational strategies including scaffold hopping based on the structure of inavolisib, -CDOCKER docking, Lipinski's rule of five, ADMET predicti
papers.summary: The authors used computational methods—scaffold hopping from the approved PI3Kα inhibitor inavolisib, molecular docking, Lipinski's rule-of-five filtering, and ADMET prediction—to identify a novel imidazole-containing compound as a candidate PI3Kα inhibitor for breast cancer. This is an in silico discovery study; the compound has not yet been experimentally validated.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Fluorinated Benzoylthiourea Derivatives: Structural Characterization, Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, Antioxidant Activity, and MAO-B Inhibitory Potential for Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives, namely FBTU1-FBTU3, were successfully synthesized in 79-86% yields and fully characterized using spectroscopic techniques including FT-IR, 1H, 13C and 19F NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). All three compounds crystallize in the monoclinic system (P21/c for FBTU1 and FBTU3; P21/n for FBTU2) with Z = 4. The crystallographic analysis revealed well-defined molecular geometries stabilized by intramolecular and intermolecular interactions. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses ind
papers.summary: The authors synthesized three new fluorinated benzoylthiourea compounds and characterized them using spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography, revealing their crystal packing and intermolecular interactions via Hirshfeld surface analysis. They also evaluated these compounds for antioxidant activity and MAO-B inhibition, a target relevant to Parkinson's disease. The work is a combined experimental and computational structure-activity study of a small set of synthetic compounds.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Identification and Experimental Validation of COX-2 and ERK1/2 as Anti-Inflammatory Targets of Avenanthramides.
papers.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation underlies numerous chronic diseases, yet the molecular targets of dietary bioactive compounds remain largely unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning to predict molecular targets of avenanthramides, oat-derived polyphenols with anti-inflammatory properties, and experimentally validates COX-2 and ERK1/2 as direct targets. The work demonstrates a combined computational and experimental pipeline for identifying protein targets of dietary bioactive compounds, which could accelerate nutraceutical discovery.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.
papers.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50-0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 an
papers.summary: The authors docked 2070 approved drugs against four E. coli antibacterial targets (FabI, LpxC, DHFR, GyrB) and then used 100 ns triplicate molecular dynamics simulations to triage top hits. Docking failed to recover known reference inhibitors (e.g., trimethoprim ranked 762nd for DHFR), highlighting scoring-function limitations, but MD refinement nominated capmatinib, metergoline, and nilotinib as candidates for experimental testing. The work is a computational repurposing screen with no experimental validation yet.

papers.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
papers.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present a descriptor-free, language-inspired deep learning framework for predicting small-molecule toxicity. It uses a multiscale CNN to capture chemical patterns at different scales within a unified architecture applicable to multiple toxicity prediction tasks. This approach aims to overcome limitations of predefined molecular descriptors and fingerprints in capturing complex structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: TopoLIA: Topology-Inspired Latent Interaction Attention for Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: The growing sophistication of drug discovery calls for new advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Transformers have underpinned recent breakthroughs in AI, yet their conventional source-target attention mechanism can become a bottleneck for modeling complex interactions. Here, we introduce TopoLIA, a topology-inspired latent interaction attention mechanism that learns not only how much information should be exchanged between interaction partners, but also how that information should be transformed. Source-target-dependent attention is mediated through a compact latent interaction space, pro
papers.summary: TopoLIA introduces a new attention mechanism for transformer models that uses a topology-inspired latent interaction space to model how information is exchanged and transformed between interacting partners, rather than just how much is exchanged. This is aimed at improving AI models for drug discovery, where complex molecular interactions are hard to capture with standard attention. The work is a methodological contribution from arXiv, likely with preliminary benchmarking.

papers.title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication. Using high-content screening in a DENV infection model, we characterized the morphological pattern
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint applies high-content morphological profiling combined with a pseudotime framework to screen a drug-repurposing library for dengue virus inhibitors. The authors use machine learning to characterize morphological patterns in DENV-infected cells and identify candidate antivirals likely to block viral replication. The work offers a scalable screening strategy for a disease that currently lacks approved antiviral treatments.

papers.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate.
papers.abstract: More than 90% of rare diseases lack an approved therapy, partly reflecting economic barriers in developing treatments for small patient populations. A common bottleneck is costly and resource-intensive hit-to-lead prioritization. Congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (CLIFAHDD) is an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disease often caused by de novo gain-of-function variants in the sodium leak channel NALCN, with no approved treatments.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes an AI-enabled drug discovery pipeline for CLIFAHDD, an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by gain-of-function mutations in the NALCN sodium leak channel. The framework spans high-throughput screening through hit-to-lead prioritization to a nominated therapeutic candidate, aiming to reduce the cost and resource burden that typically blocks treatment development for small patient populations.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Integrated Proteome-Wide Target Prioritization for Drug Discovery against Multidrug-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
papers.abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes ∼82.4 million infections annually and is rapidly approaching an untreatable status. The pathogen has developed resistance to every antibiotic class introduced since the sulfonamide era. Ceftriaxone, the last WHO- and CDC-recommended empirical therapy, is now compromised by high-level resistance in extensively drug-resistant lineages reported across multiple continents. No licensed vaccine exists, and no antibiotic with a novel mechanism has been introduced for this pathogen in over 40 years. Conventional drug discovery is too slow and insufficiently resistance-awar
papers.summary: The authors present an AI-integrated, proteome-wide pipeline to prioritize potential drug targets in multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a pathogen that has developed resistance to every antibiotic class and is approaching untreatable status. By combining computational target assessment across the full proteome, the work aims to accelerate resistance-aware target selection for a pathogen with no licensed vaccine and no new-mechanism antibiotic in over 40 years.

papers.title: Senescence-Associated Transcriptome Reversal Prioritizes Repurposing Candidates for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Computational Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease, and cellular senescence is a tractable therapeutic target; yet prioritizing credible repurposing candidates is difficult because bulk-tissue senescence signals are weak, single-dataset analyses are unstable, and transcriptome-reversal screens overstate novelty. The objective was to build a senescence-anchored, multi-evidence computational prioritization of repurposing candidates for DKD entirely from open data. Methods: Per-sample senescence activity was quantified by single-sample gene set enr
papers.summary: This computational study integrates multiple open transcriptomic datasets to build a senescence-anchored drug repurposing pipeline for diabetic kidney disease. By quantifying per-sample senescence activity and using transcriptome-reversal screening combined with multi-evidence prioritization, the authors identify candidate drugs that may reverse senescence-associated gene expression patterns in DKD. The work emphasizes methodological rigor to address instability and overstatement of novelty common in single-dataset reversal screens.

papers.title: Validated Semantic Scoring Improves Filtering of Generic Concepts from Knowledge Graphs for Drug Repurposing Queries.
papers.abstract: When an ontology-based biomedical knowledge graph (a KG, containing information about genes, pathways, phenotypes, and molecular interactions) is analyzed using a computational reasoning system, the system can return unwanted generic concepts. Such generic concepts, in the context of a query about potential drug treatments for a disease, might include 'pharmaceutical preparations' or 'antibiotics'. Answers can be filtered based on hand-curated block-lists or ontology Information Content (IC), but to our knowledge, (1) neither filtering method has been validated against expert judgments of gene
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a validated semantic scoring method to filter out overly generic concepts (like 'pharmaceutical preparations') that knowledge-graph reasoning systems return when querying for drug repurposing candidates. The authors show that their scoring approach outperforms existing hand-curated block-lists and ontology information content (IC) filtering, as validated against expert judgments. This improves the precision of ontology-based drug repurposing queries.

papers.title: Hybrid Mechanistic-Neural Modeling of Concentration-Time Dynamics Generalizes Human Pharmacokinetics Prediction Across Unseen Chemical Space.
papers.abstract: The pharmacokinetics concentration-time profile encodes ADME dynamics. Its optimization in drug discovery curbs late-stage attrition, yet forecasting human pharmacokinetics from chemical structure remains difficult. Machine learning models ignore continuous ADME dynamics, whereas physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK) models demand unavailable parameters and impose rigid, misspecified compartmental structures. We present PK-MUSE ( P harmaco K inetic hybrid M echanistic U niversal S ystem E quation), augmenting a two-compartment model with bounded, state- and time-dependent neural correc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PK-MUSE, a hybrid model that combines a two-compartment pharmacokinetic framework with neural network corrections to predict human concentration-time profiles directly from chemical structure. This approach aims to capture continuous ADME dynamics while generalizing to unseen chemical space, addressing limitations of both pure machine learning and rigid PBPK models.

papers.title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Molecular Docking Insights into Repurposing Proton Pump Inhibitors for the TLR4/MD-2, NLRP3, and C5aR1 Axes in Autoimmune Liver Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs), including autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, may include treatment-resistant cases and therefore require new therapeutic strategies. This in silico study evaluated proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) across three pathophysiologically complementary inflammatory targets relevant to hepatic immune injury: TLR4/MD-2, representing upstream innate immune sensing; NLRP3, representing inflammasome-mediated inflammatory amplification; and C5aR1, representing complement-dependent leukocyte recruitment
papers.summary: This in silico docking study tested proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) against three inflammation-related targets (TLR4/MD-2, NLRP3, and C5aR1) implicated in autoimmune liver diseases, exploring drug repurposing potential. The work is computational only, with no experimental validation, so it provides hypotheses about binding affinity rather than demonstrated therapeutic effect.

papers.title: Drugging the Undruggable in Oncology: Structural Computation, Machine Learning, and Generative AI for Historically Intractable Targets.
papers.abstract: For four decades the central oncogenic drivers of human cancer the RAS GTPases, the transcription-factor MYC, mutant p53, and the protein-tyrosine phosphatases, fusion oncoproteins and intrinsically disordered regulators that surround them were regarded as undruggable: lacking deep, well-defined small-molecule binding pockets, governed by femtomolar substrate affinities, or driven through flat protein-protein interfaces that classical medicinal chemistry could not engage. The last decade has overturned that verdict. This narrative review argues that the convergence of three advances has made t
papers.summary: This narrative review argues that historically undruggable cancer targets like RAS, MYC, and mutant p53 are now becoming tractable through the convergence of structural computation, machine learning, and generative AI. It surveys how these computational approaches are being applied to targets lacking deep binding pockets or governed by flat protein-protein interfaces, and makes the case that the 'undruggable' label is being overturned.

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantaan Virus Infection in Endothelial Cells: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Mechanistic ODE Simulations.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein-protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58.
papers.summary: The authors built a three-stage computational pipeline to find existing drugs that could be repurposed against Hantaan virus, which currently has no approved antiviral therapy. Using transcriptomic data from infected human endothelial cells, they found interferon signaling dominates the response and identified 15 hub genes (including ISG15, IRF1, STAT1, and DDX58) via protein-interaction network centrality analysis, then used mechanistic ODE simulations to probe candidate drug mechanisms.

papers.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug pert
papers.summary: This study compared primary breast tumor transcriptomes between patients with and without circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in their blood, using RNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses. It identified gene expression signatures and pathways that distinguish CTC-negative from CTC-positive tumors, linking CTC status to metastatic programs and survival outcomes. The work suggests that CTC status reflects distinct systemic remodeling in the primary tumor and may inform prognostic or therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Incensole Acetate Regulates the Sirtuin-Insulin Signaling Axis in an Experimental Alzheimer's Disease Model.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is associated with impaired brain insulin signaling, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. This study investigated the effects of incensole acetate (IA) on sirtuin-associated insulin-signaling and cellular stress-response pathways using integrated computational and in vitro approaches. Methods: ADMET prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-PBSA analyses were performed for IA against SIRT1, SIRT3, and SIRT6 and compared with their corresponding reference ligands. An Aβ1-42-induced AD model was established in mesenc
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to predict that incensole acetate binds SIRT1, SIRT3, and SIRT6, then tests it in an Aβ1-42-induced in vitro Alzheimer's model, finding modulation of sirtuin-insulin signaling and stress-response pathways. The work suggests a potential neuroprotective mechanism for this compound, though validation is limited to computational predictions and cell-based assays.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Screening Bioactive Compounds in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Computational Prediction, Multi-Omics Integration, and Clinical Translation Potential.
papers.abstract: Identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) requires computational prioritization to be connected with chemical and pharmacological evidence. This structured narrative and critical review examines machine learning applications in compound prediction, formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug development and repurposing. Molecular fingerprints, graph and sequence representations, knowledge graphs, and generative models are discussed in relation to their intended endpoints and validation conditions. Studies are classified along two independent di
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning approaches for identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine, covering molecular representations (fingerprints, graphs, sequences), knowledge graphs, and generative models, along with formula-compatibility analysis and multi-omics integration. It critically classifies studies by their intended endpoints and validation conditions, and discusses the path toward drug development, repurposing, and clinical translation.

papers.title: In Silico Evaluation of Cyanobacteria-Derived Bioactive Compounds as Potential Monoamine Oxidase-B Inhibitors for Parkinson's Disease: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Simulation Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss and impaired motor and non-motor functions. Current therapies provide symptomatic relief but do not prevent disease progression, highlighting the need for novel neuroprotective agents. Cyanobacteria-derived bioactive compounds possess diverse pharmacological properties, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, making them potential therapeutic candidates. This study aimed to identify potential monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) targeting cyanobacterial
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen cyanobacteria-derived bioactive compounds as potential inhibitors of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B), a key drug target in Parkinson's disease. The work identifies candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to MAO-B, suggesting cyanobacterial natural products as a source for neuroprotective drug development. Findings are computational only and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Application of computational methods in the drug discovery and development of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder marked by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain, leading to cognitive decline. As the most common dementia, AD affects over 50 million individuals worldwide, with 10 million new cases each year. Despite many significant progresses in AD research fields, there is still no effective treatment. Advances in molecular modelling and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm have facilitated the application of computational methods in AD drug development, offering advantages in terms of efficiency,
papers.summary: This review surveys how computational approaches—molecular modeling and AI algorithms—are being applied to Alzheimer's disease drug discovery and development, a field that still lacks effective treatments despite affecting over 50 million people worldwide. The authors argue these methods offer efficiency advantages in identifying and optimizing candidate therapeutics targeting amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial i
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to hepatitis care, covering diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction. It highlights that AI can integrate large, heterogeneous biomedical datasets to address unmet needs in early detection and risk stratification for liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. As a review, it synthesizes existing evidence rather than presenting new primary results.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing traditional bottlenecks like long timelines, high costs, and inter-patient heterogeneity.

papers.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitors: friends or foes?
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes play a central role in the metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds, influencing drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Inhibition of these enzymes has traditionally been viewed as a major liability in drug discovery due to its association with drug-drug interactions (DDIs), toxicity, and metabolic instability. However, inhibition of specific CYP450 isoforms has emerged as a powerful therapeutic strategy in multiple disease areas, including cancer and infectious diseases. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of data and regulatory guida
papers.summary: This review examines cytochrome P450 (CYP450) inhibitors, traditionally considered a liability in drug discovery due to drug-drug interactions and toxicity, and argues they can also be valuable therapeutic agents. It surveys the dual role of CYP450 inhibition across disease areas such as cancer and infectious diseases, and discusses the relevant regulatory guidance.

papers.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration-exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions of
papers.summary: This study examines how different modes of AI use (exploration vs. exploitation) affect radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery, drawing on the exploration-exploitation framework and environmental dynamism. It proposes a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions to employee creative outcomes, arguing that AI's value for radical innovation depends on how creatively employees use it to transcend established knowledge boundaries rather than mere adoption.

papers.title: A review on advances in chemical compound toxicology prediction.
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of chemical toxicity remains a major challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment because conventional approaches can be costly, time-consuming, ethically constrained, and limited in predictive performance. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is being applied to predictive toxicology. It covers conventional algorithms such as support vector machines (SVMs), decision trees (DTs), and ensemble methods, together with advanced approaches including graph neural networks (GNNs). The
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, is being applied to predict chemical toxicity for drug development and safety assessment. It covers conventional algorithms like support vector machines, decision trees, and ensemble methods, as well as advanced approaches such as graph neural networks, highlighting the shift toward data-driven toxicology prediction.

papers.title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi.
papers.abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction-Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus stu
papers.summary: This paper presents PTI-TAPE, a consensus framework developed through a three-round eDelphi study to standardize how computational peptide-target interaction predictions are evaluated. It addresses the current lack of agreed metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction standards that make cross-study comparisons difficult and hinder clinical translation of therapeutic peptides.

papers.title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
papers.abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensio
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how the environmental pollutant 6PPD-quinone might contribute to intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways, suggesting that 6PPD-Q may activate stress-related responses (e.g., mitochondrial membrane potential and antioxidant response element) in disc tissue. The findings are computational predictions that require experimental validation.

papers.title: Redefining drug discovery: AI-driven strategies for efficient cancer therapeutics.
papers.abstract: The practice of artificial intelligence has recently expanded several social spheres, with the pharmaceutical domain leading the way. Given that AI can facilitate rational drug design, it is plausible to envision its involvement in developing pharmaceutical products from the laboratory to the patient's bedside. AI recognizes hit and lead compounds, followed by validation of therapeutic targets and optimization of molecular design. Artificial intelligence significantly impacts drug discovery and development processes, including target identification, molecule design, drug-drug interactions, dru
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is being applied across the drug discovery pipeline for cancer therapeutics, from identifying drug targets and hit/lead compounds to molecular optimization and predicting drug-drug interactions. It argues that AI can streamline rational drug design and help move candidate compounds from the lab toward clinical use. The paper is a broad overview rather than a report of new experimental results.

papers.title: Potential Molecular Links Between Benzophenone-3 and Breast Cancer: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Molecular Modeling, and Gene Expression Validation.
papers.abstract: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is a widely used ultraviolet filter with potential carcinogenic concern, but its molecular link with breast cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate targets and potential molecular links between BP-3 and breast cancer using toxicological prediction, machine learning, molecular modeling, and gene expression analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, and gene expression validation to identify candidate molecular targets linking the UV filter benzophenone-3 (BP-3) to breast cancer. The authors propose potential target genes and pathways through which BP-3 exposure might contribute to breast carcinogenesis, though the evidence is largely computational with limited experimental validation.
